verified_claims: EvoJAX is an Apache-licensed JAX neuroevolution toolkit with notebook examples and optional GPU/TPU execution.
The project notes that Colab includes JAX and provides notebooks under its examples tree.
limitations: No exact EvoJAX SNN Colab notebook matching the imported title was confirmed.
The Google repository was archived in August 2025 and is read-only.
General neuroevolution support does not establish a biologically grounded SNN simulator.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Archived general JAX neuroevolution toolkit; no verified project-specific SNN notebook.
decisions.note: The generic nbviewer link is replaced, but the imported SNN-specific identity remains unconfirmed.

verified_claims: The MIT-licensed repository contains an SNN simulator example notebook and a Colab badge.
limitations: The checked GitHub repository is a fork and explicitly labels itself legacy.
Maintenance moved to a Radboud GitLab instance; the current upstream contents and reproducibility were not verified.
No evidence establishes scalability to the target connectome.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Legacy educational SNN notebook whose maintained upstream must be checked before reuse.
decisions.note: Do not select it over maintained simulators without a local benchmark.

verified_claims: The Seung Lab FlyConnectome repository contains a 4,045-line CAVE tutorial notebook for programmatic connectome access.
limitations: The notebook documents data access, not neuronal dynamics, nociception or simulation validity.
Authentication, materialization version and API outputs must be pinned in any reproducible extraction.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Primary tutorial for programmatic CAVE/FlyConnectome data access.
decisions.note: Use with an explicit materialization/version manifest.

verified_claims: The GeNN documentation gives a Brian2GeNN LIF example with varying input currents to construct an f/I curve.
It documents switching Brian2 to the GeNN device and configuring GeNN/CUDA paths.
limitations: The page belongs to older GeNN 3 documentation and is an API example, not a current performance benchmark.
The example is too small to demonstrate benefit from GPU execution.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Legacy official Brian2GeNN interface example for an LIF f/I curve.
decisions.note: Retain as a minimal syntax example; use current package docs for environment setup.

verified_claims: The current MetaTF documentation describes akida-models, QuantizeML, CNN2SNN and the Akida runtime/software backend.
The current installation page documents Python 3.10-3.12 and versioned package dependencies.
limitations: The runtime is a vendor stack governed by BrainChip licensing, not a wholly open-source framework.
Supported Python, TensorFlow and package versions change and must be locked per experiment.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Official versioned documentation for quantization, conversion, simulation and Akida deployment.
decisions.note: Duplicate role with ST026 is retained only as documentation rather than software identity.

verified_claims: The official documentation provides tutorials, API reference, model configuration, experiment tracking, cross-validation and explainability guides.
limitations: The documentation is general-purpose and does not define participant-safe splits for pain datasets.
Specific model availability is version-dependent and must be pinned.
decisions.corrected_purpose: Official PyTorch Tabular documentation for structured-feature baselines.
decisions.note: The exact documentation URL replaces the redirected source repository link.

limitations: The imported requirement (16+ CPU cores) has no workload benchmark, dependency lock or primary source.

decisions.note: Rejected as an evidence resource, not asserted to be technically impossible.
